## 債市主線

10月20日，油價回落、美國住宅活動急遽轉弱，帶動資金重回較長天期美國公債，收復週一部分跌幅。10年期殖利率下降3.12個基點至5.1085%，30年期下降4.75個基點至5.4198%；2年期則小幅走高。殖利率曲線趨平，顯示市場並未全面撤回對聯準會進一步緊縮的預期。

這一交易日緩解的是實質借款成本，長期通膨補償並未明顯下降。油價反轉在盤中助長債市漲勢，但能源價格仍高，10年期債券隱含的通膨預期反而略升。9月新屋開工遠遜預期，成屋待完成銷售則在各地區全面收縮下跌至歷史低點，顯示高利率的抑制作用已反映在實際施工與交易。

企業信用市場並未像公債反彈那樣令人安心。投資人準備迎接新一波AI相關借款，Oracle、Meta與SpaceX的違約保護成本均創新高。Radiology Partners聯貸案受挫，Thames Water則向債權人提出新的妥協方案，反映借款人必須更換融資工具或重新分配債權，才能取得資金。不過，美國整體高收益債利差收盤仍大致持平。當日行情呈現的差別是：市場增加對利率敏感債券的需求，卻仍仔細衡量誰能籌資、必須接受什麼條件，以及由誰的資金承擔風險。

## 住宅轉弱，美債殖利率曲線趨平

原油由漲轉跌後，美債反彈加速。Bloomberg盤中報導指出，紐約時間上午8時前不久，10年期殖利率約在5.12%；其後油價回吐漲幅、一度跌逾2%，殖利率隨之降至5.08%以下。最初促使油價下跌的是一則尚未獲證實的消息，稱卡達與巴基斯坦提出新方案，試圖重啟伊朗戰爭談判。參與協商的一名外交官後來表示，談判仍在進行，但即將達成協議的報導並不正確。

美國債市收盤時，WTI下跌2.48%至每桶$101.09，Brent下跌0.36%至$109.16。兩者跌幅差異值得注意：WTI當日回落幅度較大，但兩項基準仍分別較一週前上漲7.38%與3.28%，Brent近一個月更上漲9.94%。談判消息降低了油價帶來的即時壓力，恢復供應的協議卻仍未達成。

RBC Capital Markets策略師Izaac Brook認為，買進債券的動力同時來自市場持續擔憂AI投資，以及原油走低。盤中先後順序也支持這種解讀：科技業融資疑慮已先帶動防禦性買盤，之後油價反轉才讓債市漲勢加速。半導體股自早盤低點回升，收盤仍跌0.29%，Nasdaq 100下跌0.13%；S&P 500則上漲0.28%，超過400檔成分股收高，VIX下跌6.13%至17.31。公債上漲與廣泛的股票漲勢並存，並非所有風險資產同步遭到拋售。

各天期收盤表現同樣分化。5年期殖利率下降1.08個基點至4.9291%，2年期卻上升0.42個基點至4.7761%；2年與10年期利差收窄3.54個基點至33.24個基點，2年與30年期利差收窄5.17個基點至64.37個基點。長天期反應較大，短端則仍受後續升息可能性牽制。

一週以來，10年與30年期殖利率分別下降9.99與13.71個基點，2年期僅降1.29個基點。但拉長至一個月，融資成本仍高：10年期殖利率上升11.15個基點，30年期上升9.28個基點。週二反彈減輕了這項負擔，尚未將其消除。

10年期實質殖利率下降3.27個基點至2.7503%，損益兩平通膨率則上升0.15個基點至2.3582%。一週比較亦呈現相同分歧，實質殖利率下降11.12個基點，損益兩平通膨率上升1.13個基點。因此，油價下跌雖是盤中催化劑，當日名目公債漲勢仍主要來自實質殖利率下降，而非長期通膨補償明顯回落。這也有助解釋2年期公債為何未能跟漲。

Bloomberg週二利率報導指出，即使油價下跌時交易員削減了升息預期，市場仍完全反映年底前再升息一次、明年底前累計升息三次。面對活動轉弱，市場重新評估緊縮的幅度與時點，但仍保留因應通膨而進一步升息的可能。

住宅數據最清楚地呈現了高利率的抑制效果。9月新屋開工下降5.2%，年率為122.1萬戶，低於市場預估的130萬戶，也低於8月修正後的128.8萬戶；前一個月跌幅修正為5.9%。經濟學家原本預期開工戶數會回升，實際施工卻再度收縮。

建築許可初值相對穩健，下降0.2%，由140.3萬戶降至140萬戶，仍高於預估的139萬戶；8月許可曾下降2.1%。實際動工大幅減少，核准戶數卻僅小幅下滑，顯示眼前惡化主要集中在真正開始施工的項目，許可所代表的後續供給並未同樣驟降。

交易端更為疲弱。美國全國不動產經紀人協會（NAR）的成屋待完成銷售指數下降7.3%至66，創2001年有紀錄以來最低。前次上升0.3%後，經濟學家原估本月下降0.5%，結果卻低於Bloomberg調查的所有預測。各地區簽約均減少，以西部下降9.2%及最大房屋銷售地區南部下降8.2%最為明顯。

經濟日曆所列的待完成銷售年減率為11.3%，前次年減4.7%；NAR另列的未經調整比較則顯示，簽約量較去年同期減少近13%。NAR首席經濟學家Lawrence Yun將9月惡化歸因於房貸利率快速上升，使買賣雙方都轉為觀望。簽約通常領先實際完成交易一至兩個月，這次下滑也削弱了近期成交前景。

其餘美國數據顯示成長放緩，尚未指向全面收縮。ADP每週就業增幅由24,750人降至18,500人；截至10月17日當週，Redbook零售銷售年增率由10.4%放緩至9%。亞特蘭大聯準銀行GDPNow模型對第3季成長的估計由3.6%微降至3.5%。住宅格外嚴重的疲弱，與這些較廣泛指標持續成長的情況並存。

ING的Padhraic Garvey認為，新公布的美國數據整體有利債市。美國財政部長Scott Bessent另表示，預期能源衝擊過後房貸利率將下降，並將政府擬讓房利美與房地美退出接管的時點放在明年或後年。不過，9月的融資成本已使住宅施工與購屋縮減，這些前景尚未為借款人帶來即時紓解。

## AI融資壓力蔓延至最大發債企業

即使美國長債殖利率下降，科技業信用仍走弱。Bloomberg引述ICE Data Services數據指出，Oracle的信用違約交換（CDS）週二最高升至343個基點，創歷史新高。Meta在週三財報公布前，信用風險指標最多上升6.3個基點至114.8個基點新高。SpaceX的5年期違約保護成本週二早盤一度觸及242個基點紀錄，相較之下，其CDS在6月開始活躍交易時約為111個基點。

市場共同擔心的是下一輪融資的規模。Pimco策略師Lotfi Karoui表示，投資人對債市究竟需要吸收多少AI建設借款，尚無定論。Bloomberg統計，今年全球用於AI融資的借款已超過$4,500億。企業準備走出財報靜默期之際，既有債券持有人正為潛在新券騰出空間，並非只是對已公布營收立即惡化作出反應。

美國銀行分析師估計，交易商週一淨買入$4.51億大型雲端業者債券，為9月中旬以來最大增持量；他們認為，庫存增加很可能反映投資人因擔心供給而減碼。投資人預期Meta可能在未來幾天發債，結束大型科技企業美元發債逾兩個月的空窗。SpaceX則正與銀行及投資人洽談$400億融資，用於購買Nvidia晶片；該公司6月首次發行高評級債券時，已籌得$250億。

Meta財報訂於10月21日公布，比2022年以來慣常的當月最後一個週三提早，引發市場猜測公司有意保留11月期中選舉前的融資窗口。CreditSights分析師Jordan Chalfin先前已提出，財報後可能有大規模發債。公司未回應置評要求。

避險交易也反映出相關曝險擴大的程度。Barclays策略師Jigar Patel分析交易資料儲存庫後指出，截至9月，與十大雲端及晶片企業連結的CDS交易額達創紀錄的$1,400億，較2025年同期約$177億增加691%；部分合約才剛開始交易。普信投資組合經理人Steven Kohlenstein表示，融資需求攀升，讓投資人更注意過去被視為各自獨立信用風險的企業，其曝險其實彼此相關。

當日新的股票跌勢來自韓國運算服務供應商Elice，首爾上市首日股價重挫32%。公司已有政府合約、營運中的資料中心且具獲利，仍受到市場重新評估新興雲端業者融資的衝擊，壓力因而不只限於首批專案尚未投入營運的企業。CoreWeave股價週二回升，但其債務與擴張融資成本的疑慮，仍持續影響市場對該產業的態度。

融資時程延後的跡象也增加。Blackstone支持的AirTrunk在美國9月升息後，將原擬為規模$15億的新加坡不動產投資信託進行的投資人會談延至明年；該擬議工具原預期提供約6%殖利率。SB Energy的IPO洽談則因監管核准耗時超出預期而明顯放慢。澳洲市場監管機關正在蒐集Firmus Grid取消IPO的相關資訊，但尚未展開正式調查。

半導體當前獲利強勁，估值卻低迷，兩者落差同時擴大。週二韓股報導指出，Kospi較6月歷史高點下跌近40%，Samsung與SK Hynix則分別較當時高點下跌40%與56%；兩家公司合計占指數市值近一半。Samsung最新一季獲利達創紀錄的$800億，股價卻不到預估全年獲利的5倍；SK Hynix不到4倍，兩者本益比均約為過去十年平均的一半。投資人質疑的是客戶支出能支撐這些獲利多久，而不是否認當前記憶體需求。

美股收盤後，SpaceX公布單季淨利$44億，高於分析師平均預估的$18.8億，AI與衛星網路業務均成長。後續報導另指出，SpaceX與Tesla已成立特別委員會，探討合併可能性。這份獲利為當日創高的違約保護成本提供了營運面上的對照，特別委員會則啟動了另一項初步企業程序。

紐約時間下午5時35分發布的較晚更新中，Bloomberg轉述《華爾街日報》報導，Anthropic未來幾年可能為增加運算能力投入$7,500億。《華爾街日報》引述IPO招股書草稿，另稱公司2026年上半年淨損$807億。在Anthropic計畫上市之前，這項未來支出規模與已發生虧損，於債市收盤後進一步增添融資議題。

## 法國融資成本上升，日本買盤回溫

核心公債普遍回升，法國公債卻再度逆勢。週二盤中，法國10年期公債相對德國的利差突破150個基點、達到154個基點，法債殖利率再度逼近5%。利差雖仍低於本月159個基點高點，重新擴大仍顯示，街頭抗議平息並未解除主權財政壓力。

宵禁與加強維安使示威大致平息，但削減支出的阻力仍是政府融資困境的核心。Morningstar DBRS保險業主管Marcos Alvarez估計，暴動損失目前仍將低於€12億。法國一方面試圖控制赤字，一方面必須回應生活成本訴求，這項估計為週末動盪增添了新的損失衡量。

歐洲央行管理委員會成員Olli Rehn週二向芬蘭國會議員表示，利差擴大同時來自國際與個別國家壓力：包括AI投資在內的民間資本需求，以及擴大的公共赤字，都推高了資金成本。他認為，法國、芬蘭等每個歐元區國家都必須控制赤字，以確保債務可持續性。這番談話著重財政調整，並未承諾支持法債。

BlackRock Investment Institute的Wei Li及同事也將法債跌勢視為資金競爭加劇的證據。他們的比較顯示，全球超過80%的債券殖利率高於4%，五年前僅6.3%，借款人面對的競爭性投資選項因而大幅增加。研究所也強調，相較先前主權債危機，歐元區銀行更健全，歐洲央行可用工具也更有力，但介入並無保證。法國債務接近GDP的120%，歐元區整體約為89%。

Bessent週二表示，他不預期法國動盪會外溢至美債，並稱已看到資金從較令人擔憂的市場流向美國公債。德國與英國公債也在美國交易時段上漲，Bloomberg較晚的市場報導指出，兩國10年期殖利率分別下降6個基點至3.40%、下降2個基點至5.41%。其他市場回升時法國利差仍擴大，使其國別因素更加鮮明。

英國最新交易商調查則量化了即將到來的供給決策。11份預測的中位數顯示，截至3月的年度英國公債發行量將為£2,492億，較4月公布的£2,462億增加£30億，預估範圍介於£2,430億至£2,562億。債務成本與支出需求上升，即使提高銀行稅等措施可抵銷部分壓力，交易商仍預期財政餘裕將縮減約三分之一至£152億，壓縮政府調度空間。

供給結構的預期變化，比公債總量增幅更明顯。交易商估計國庫券發行量為£111億，高於4月計畫的£50億；短期與中期公債占公債發行比重分別為42.7%與35.3%，高於原先39%與31%；長天期比重則由9%降至6.5%。美國銀行策略師Agne Stengeryte與Mark Capleton認為，若更大幅調整期限組合，將更能使供給符合需求。這些是對首相Andy Burnham與財政大臣John Healey於10月28日提出預算及融資計畫的預測。

日本呈現的則是已實現的需求，而非預期中的供給修正。週二20年期日本公債標售投標倍數達5.84倍，創歷史新高，高於前次4.01倍與過去十二個月平均3.73倍。之後20年期殖利率最多下降6個基點至3.710%，30年期最多下降5個基點。近期承壓尤其明顯的長天期市場，開始以較高殖利率吸引買盤。

買方身分仍有不同解讀，超過83%的投標來自未具名投資人。BNP Paribas Asset Management的Ryutaro Kimura認為，這可能意味大型機構參與，包括大型銀行與日本政府年金投資基金（GPIF）。德意志證券的Shoki Omori則提到，壽險與退休基金透過信託銀行買進、地方銀行受到票息吸引，以及交易商回補空頭。Bloomberg策略師Mark Cranfield認為可能有外資參與。GPIF不評論個別投資活動。Kimura也提醒，銀行可能趁殖利率下降賣出，近期股市下跌則可能限制退休基金進一步再平衡的需求。

另行公布的數據揭示了先前國內買盤規模。截至9月30日的六個月，日本投資人淨買入公債¥18.8兆，為十七年來最高的會計年度上半年總額；信託銀行占近一半，銀行占約三分之一。三菱UFJ摩根士丹利證券策略師Keisuke Tsuruta將信託銀行大量買進，主要歸因於股市上漲與日圓走弱改變投資組合權重後，公共退休基金進行再平衡。

外債數據則顯示，增加日債配置的投資人，對海外資產的買賣方向並不一致。同一半年期間，信託帳戶買入¥10.1兆外債，銀行卻賣出¥7.4兆，為至少2014年以來最大減碼。Tsuruta認為，銀行賣出與預期高油價將推升美國及歐洲公債殖利率有關。週二公布的資料區分了銀行與退休基金相關投資人的行為，即使兩者都增加了日債需求。

## 政策與主權融資各走不同路徑

中國對隔夜政策基準的討論，推進到具體操作期間。中國人民銀行宣布，將於10月21日至11月2日進行隔夜逆回購，不再僅側重過去的月底與繳稅期間，為擬議中由7天期基準轉向隔夜基準提供了實際下一步。

法國興業銀行經濟學家Michelle Lam認為，更頻繁的隔夜操作可讓央行測試傳導效果，並降低短期利率波動。天風證券Liu Jie率領的分析團隊預期，隔夜利率將在2027年上半年成為正式基準；南華期貨研究員Gao Xiang則表示，完成轉換前仍需提高操作頻率與定價透明度。

這是否意味寬鬆，市場仍有分歧。分析師認為，較低的融資利率基準可能提高債券利息收益扣除融資成本後的收益，鼓勵投資人買進較長天期債券，但更可靠的隔夜再融資也可能增加槓桿與期限錯配。中國1年期利率交換降至2009年以來最低。不過，人行旗下《金融時報》週二文章引述廣發證券經濟學家Guo Lei指出，操作架構改革不應等同降息。

匈牙利則實際按兵不動，連續第二個月維持基準利率5.5%，符合Bloomberg調查全部22名經濟學家的預期。央行總裁Mihaly Varga認為，政府財政路徑與最終加入歐元區的目標一致，並重申審慎、依據數據決策的政策立場。政府計畫將明年赤字目標訂為GDP的4.9%，2030年降至2.8%。總理Peter Magyar表示應儘快採用歐元，但未設定日期。

投資人已提前反映大幅財政整頓及加入單一貨幣的進展，因此預算案引發的市場反應有限。9月通膨為1.6%，低於央行2%至4%的容忍區間；財政可信度與福林走勢，因而攸關能否恢復寬鬆。Varga表示，包括加入ERM-2匯率機制在內的後續步驟，仍須由政府決定。

波蘭貨幣政策委員Marcin Zarzecki則提出少見的具體升息條件。他不預期11月升息，但也不排除；若核心通膨連續兩個月高於3.5%、薪資增幅超過7%、茲羅提貶至每歐元4.5以上，三者中有兩項成立，就值得認真考慮升息25個基點。三項全數成立時，可能支持連續升息或單次較大幅度調升。他另指出，取消燃油價格上限或調高2027年家庭能源費率，是額外的政治風險。

最新數據尚未觸及這些門檻：核心通膨3.1%，8月薪資增幅5.6%，週一匯率為每歐元4.37茲羅提。Zarzecki表示，他的看法與央行總裁Adam Glapinski一致，與另一位委員Przemyslaw Litwiniuk上週認為茲羅提仍強的判斷形成對照。他也警告，針對Glapinski的程序可能使政策決策遭到法律挑戰；總裁則駁斥政治干預指控毫無根據。

印尼眼前的政策壓力不同。截至週二較晚時，38名經濟學家中有19名預期週三將調高目前5.75%的基準利率，其中17名預估升息25個基點，兩名預估50個基點。預測轉變，源自MSCI警告可能重新分類後的匯率與債市壓力。當局承諾改革後，印尼股市週二反彈，雅加達指數最多上漲4.3%。交易所表示，與MSCI討論後，股權高度集中的公司將不納入基準指數計算，但持股透明度與協同行為交易疑慮仍在。

塞內加爾美元債則因既定融資路徑遇到新阻礙而下跌。週二倫敦時間下午2時45分，2031年到期債下跌2.10美分至每1美元面額49.99美分；2033年與2048年到期債最多跌2美分。國會議長兼反對派領袖Ousmane Sonko威脅，不批准修正後的2026年預算與明年支出計畫，反對為在2028年前將燃油補貼壓至GDP的1%而削減補貼。

Sonko所屬Pastef黨掌握國會多數，爭議將直接影響法案通過。塞內加爾正依G20共同框架重整外部債務，並爭取IMF董事會批准上月原則同意的$22億融資。渣打銀行Samir Gadio將該國債券表現落後歸因於預算不確定性。預算部長Bassirou Sarr則以能源成本上升，以及保護薪資和既有社會承諾的必要性，為計畫辯護。融資時程如今面臨的是落實調整的政治障礙，而不只是對調整數字是否足夠的歧見。

巴西正在準備另一條融資管道。知情人士指出，官員正在中國籌辦首次熊貓債發行，最快下週啟動，目標約人民幣100億元，首批人民幣50億元，將使巴西成為首個進入該市場的拉丁美洲主權發行人。巴西國庫部門表示，尚無確定日期，是否發行取決於市場條件與需求。

可能的發行時點落在10月25日總統決選之後。熟悉籌備的人士預期，即使Flavio Bolsonaro勝選，首筆交易仍會推進，但他與總統Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva對長期擴大在中國發債的策略可能不同。另有熟悉計畫的人士指出，Vale也在考慮人民幣債，無論選舉結果如何都打算繼續。巴西政府今年已在國際市場籌得約$100億，並尋求每年最多$350億的發債授權，中國市場的準備工作因此屬於外部借款多元化的一環。

羅馬尼亞則在週二由Luca Niculescu取得國會對新內閣的批准，結束數月政治僵局。這位5月以來第四名獲提名的總理，如今必須維持財政紀律、說服信評機構，並在僵局拖累匯率後重振成長。信任投票解決了組閣問題，財政計畫仍待落實。

## 再融資條件凸顯信用分化

知情人士指出，Radiology Partners撤回原擬增額發行的$4.85億2032年到期貸款，改向市場推介非投資等級債券，討論中的殖利率最高10.25%，相較Bloomberg追蹤的同評級債券平均為8.38%。撤回的貸款曾提出最高高於基準利率475個基點的加碼利差，以及最低每1美元面額98美分的發行價格；前者是浮動利率貸款的加碼利差與折價發行條件，後者則是替代債券的整體殖利率。

這筆收購融資進一步顯示聯貸承作受阻。Grant Thornton Advisors週一將等值$5億的歐元貸款改為債券，AVI-SPL撤回$6.9億再融資；Envestnet週二則必須改善一筆$6.25億貸款的條件，以支應收購Vestmark。借款人原本看重貸款可再融資、無須承擔債券式提前贖回罰則的彈性，但需求轉弱與浮動利率債務償付負擔，正使交易更難完成。

部分投資人並未全面放棄企業信用，而是轉向研究高收益債中評級最高的一群。普信與景順在近期跌勢後考慮BB級債，經理人著重現金創造能力、利潤率與較低槓桿。報導引述S&P數據，BB借款人三年累計違約率4.17%，相較BBB為0.91%、B為12.41%、CCC為45.67%。Moody’s研究則發現，未來兩年到期的高收益債中，財務困難借款人約占三分之一。這些比較解釋了投資人偏向BB債的品質區別，而當日美國整體高收益債利差大致持平。

PLS證明市場仍可發債。這家澳洲鋰生產商以面額發行$7億2032年到期債，殖利率8%，資金用於一般企業用途，包括投資與成長。本月稍早，公司已批准A$19億擴建案，目標使Pilgangoora產能接近倍增。Moody’s週二給予Ba3評級，指出施工期間現金流為負、債務增加，以及鋰價疲弱帶來的曝險上升。公司4月在不同融資環境下首次發行美元債，票息為6.875%。

CIBC也將先前推介中的發行落實。知情人士指出，該行週一售出C$10億其他第一類資本有限追索權資本票據，相對公債利差297個基點，票息6.631%，共有43名買方。票據期限60年，約五年後首次可贖回，此後每五年有一次贖回機會，提前償還須獲監管批准。Bloomberg Intelligence的Himanshu Bakshi提醒，銀行正衡量替代融資成本、資本需求與重設利差，票據未於可贖回日贖回而延續的風險正在升高。

Pernod Ricard尋求以不同方式支撐資產負債表，啟動首次混合資本債投資人電話會議，並對合計€47億的七檔優先順位歐元債提出設有總額上限的收購要約。擬議中的永續債分兩批，首次可贖回日分別在5.25年與八年後。其淨負債對EBITDA為3.7倍，目標在2029會計年度降至3倍以下；Moody’s的Baa1與S&P的BBB+優先債評級，展望均為負向。混合資本債預期評級分別為Baa3與BBB-，信評機構給予部分權益認列是方案的重要因素。目前市場混合資本債相對優先債利差為61個基點，接近歷史低點，低於超過120個基點的長期平均。

Thames Water與支持方案的債權人，向Pimco提出新增£24億紓困債務的修正版分配方案。首批£6億將按比例分給超優先順位、A類與B類債權人，其餘£18億再分配給擴大後的超優先順位債權人群體。相較原方案，Pimco與其他既有最高順位貸款人可取得更大份額，以回應整筆融資擴至£54億時，其權益遭稀釋的疑慮。

這項融資票息9.75%，另加費用，目前交易價格高於面額。Thames表示，新增資金可維持營運至2027年秋季。分配妥協旨在10月29日表決前爭取債權人支持；若所需多數提前批准，表決可提早結束。A類債權人另提的資本重整與接管計畫，仍須說服監管機關與政府，政府則曾考慮特別管理程序。此次新提案聚焦於取得紓困資金，以及其優先債權的分配。

Vestel提出重整方案，讓債券持有人直接在本金與期限間選擇。持有人可將$5億2029年到期債中的最多$2.5億，按每1美元本金換取55美分的2032年到期債，票息6%，接受45%本金減記；或保留本金，將到期日延至2035年、利息降至4%。11月11日會議須取得出席代表債券至少75%的支持。這家土耳其家電製造商在獲利轉弱、流動性承壓之際，也正另行協商國內銀行債務。

Huachen Energy披露，12月到期的$9.56億債務償還有困難，並在週五債權人電話會議中歸因於獲利不如預期、資產出售受阻，以及母公司永泰能源援助有限。公司先前已重整，如今尋求再展延六年，計畫本週與個別債權人會談。相關債務包括約$6.27億美元票據與人民幣22億元債券；最新方案將再次延後2021年違約後已獲展延的付款期限。

WestJet票息8%、2031年到期債週二上午約報每1美元面額85美分，較週一下跌約3%，創6月發行以來最低，10月初約為95美分。高燃油成本、美加貿易不確定性，以及8月空服員罷工的干擾，持續壓抑前景；S&P已於9月將其降評至B-。澳洲方面，Ares主管Peter Graf另警告，浮動利率不動產貸款壓力增加，目前優先順位不動產貸款成本可能達11%至12%，六個月前為8%至9%。他與Blackstone的Mark Glengarry都不預期發生系統性信用緊縮，將個別不動產曝險的壓力，與區域整體信用前景作出區分。

市政債交易顯示，部分較小借款人仍能順利融資。Chapin School發言人指出，學校為$2,500萬再融資定價，相對基準利差47個基點，需求達最初發行量五倍。另有$2,500萬到期款項將以自有資金償還，合計$5,000萬到期債務處理後，未償債務將減少三分之一。學校評級A+、投資組合$1.28億，入學需求強勁；雖有營運赤字，校方主要歸因於$1,300萬非現金折舊。安大略國際機場則在Fitch將其債務連升兩級至A+後，計畫發行約$1.74億債券，用於航廈與跑道工程，其中約$1.24億適用替代性最低稅。

## 後續市場觀察

週三房貸申請將在9月住宅收縮之外，提供較近期的融資需求資料。前次MBA調查顯示，30年期房貸利率7.5%，申請量下降2.7%。週四初領失業救濟金人數預估20萬人、續領預估172萬人，可在ADP每週就業增幅放慢之後，延伸觀察勞動市場。重點是住宅劇烈惡化仍集中在最利率敏感的活動，還是伴隨更廣泛的動能流失。

10月21日20年期美債標售與10月22日5年期TIPS標售，將檢驗長債上漲、實質殖利率下降後的需求。名目債與通膨連結債買方面對的曝險不同：週二實質殖利率下降時，10年期損益兩平通膨率幾乎未動。同時，潛在科技業發債將競逐資金；Meta週三財報將提供最新支出資訊，也可能開啟新一輪借款窗口。

週五10月S&P Global PMI初值將擴大對景氣的評估。製造業市場預估55.5，前值55.9；服務業預估58，前值58.8。密西根大學調查終值的一年與五年通膨預期，市場分別預估4.7%與3.5%。若活動持續成長、通膨預期偏高，聯準會面對的權衡，將不同於景氣全面放緩且物價預期下降的情境，尤其短端週二未跟隨長債上漲。

能源仍能獨立改變上述判斷。API週二下午公布原油庫存減少493萬桶，降幅大於預期130萬桶，前次修正為減少1,112萬桶。週三EIA原油庫存預估減少30萬桶。外交談判持續之際，歐洲天然氣週二另發出警訊：荷蘭基準期貨最多上漲2.4%至每兆瓦時€90.16，為2022年12月以來最高。Ryanair執行長Michael O’Leary預估，燃油成本轉嫁可能使明年票價最多上漲20%，多數歐洲航空公司對該期間並無大規模避險。

印尼央行將於週三雅加達時間下午2時公布決策，經濟學家對是否升息各占一半。當局處理股市治理的根本疑慮之際，除了利率決策本身，印尼盾與公債反應也很重要。韓國週四決策則有不同焦點：受訪24名經濟學家全數預期維持3%，但Citi與Nomura認為其後仍會升向3.5%。9月整體與核心通膨分別為2.9%與2.8%，仍高於2%目標。總裁Shin Hyun Song如何評估股市重挫與半導體出口強勁並存的局面，以及是否有委員主張立即升息，將影響11月預期。

英國10月28日預算將把交易商的新預測轉為實際借款計畫與期限組合。法國利差再度擴大，顯示即使抗議平息，財政共識與回應生活成本壓力的政治問題仍未解。日本標售已證明高殖利率能吸引需求，但買盤來源的不同解釋，也使其持續性取決於國內機構如何因應後續行情。這些市場下一步融資條件的變化，將來自具體供給決策、政策選擇與債權人協議，而不只是美債殖利率方向。

overall_summary.headline: 住宅轉弱、油價回落帶動美國長債反彈，企業融資壓力仍在
overall_summary.session_narrative:
油價回落，9月住宅數據也顯示高借款成本正壓抑施工與交易，較長天期美債因而收復週一部分跌幅。10年期殖利率下降3.12個基點至5.1085%，30年期下降4.75個基點至5.4198%，2年期則上升0.42個基點至4.7761%。2年與10年期利差收窄3.54個基點至33.24個基點。這波漲勢來自實質殖利率下降：10年期實質殖利率下降3.27個基點至2.7503%，損益兩平通膨率反而上升0.15個基點至2.3582%。

新屋開工下降5.2%，年率為122.1萬戶；成屋待完成銷售下跌7.3%，指數降至歷史低點66。油價反轉加速債市回升，但伊朗戰爭談判尚未達成協議，能源價格仍高。市場仍完全反映聯準會年底前再升息一次。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Longer-dated Treasuries rallied on October 20 as falling oil prices and a sharp deterioration in U.S. housing activity restored demand for government debt, reversing part of Monday's selloff. The 10-year yield declined 3.12 basis points to 5.1085%, and the 30-year fell 4.75 basis points to 5.4198%. The two-year yield edged higher, leaving a flatter curve rather than a market-wide retreat from expectations of further Federal Reserve tightening.

The session brought relief in real borrowing costs, not a meaningful decline in long-term inflation compensation. Oil's reversal helped bonds during the day, but energy remained expensive and inflation expectations embedded in 10-year securities were slightly higher. September housing starts fell well short of expectations, while pending home sales reached a record low across a broad regional contraction. Those releases showed the restraint from high interest rates reaching actual construction and transactions.

Corporate credit presented a less reassuring picture than the recovery in government bonds. Default-protection costs for Oracle, Meta and SpaceX reached records as investors prepared for another wave of AI-related borrowing. A failed loan syndication at Radiology Partners and a new creditor compromise at Thames Water showed borrowers having to change instruments or redistribute claims to secure financing. Broad U.S. high-yield spreads nevertheless finished little changed. The day's distinction was between stronger demand for duration and continuing scrutiny of who could raise money, on what terms, and with whose capital at risk.

## Housing Weakens as the Treasury Curve Flattens

The Treasury recovery gathered pace as crude reversed an earlier advance. Bloomberg's intraday account put the 10-year yield near 5.12% shortly before 8 a.m. in New York, then below 5.08% as oil erased its gain and briefly dropped more than 2%. An unconfirmed report of a fresh proposal from Qatar and Pakistan to revive negotiations over the Iran war helped trigger the initial oil retreat. A diplomat involved in the negotiations subsequently said talks continued but reports that an agreement was close were inaccurate.

By the completed U.S. bond session, WTI was down 2.48% at $101.09 a barrel and Brent had slipped 0.36% to $109.16. The different magnitudes matter: WTI's retreat was substantial for the day, but both benchmarks remained above their levels a week earlier, with gains of 7.38% and 3.28%, respectively. Brent was still 9.94% higher over the month. Negotiation headlines reduced the immediate pressure from oil without delivering an agreed restoration of supply.

RBC Capital Markets strategist Izaac Brook attributed the rates buying to both continuing concern about AI investment and the move lower in crude. The chronology supported that combination. Anxiety over technology financing had already encouraged defensive demand before oil's reversal accelerated the rally. Semiconductor shares recovered from early losses but still finished 0.29% lower, while the Nasdaq 100 lost 0.13%. The broader S&P 500 rose 0.28%, with more than 400 constituents advancing, and the VIX fell 6.13% to 17.31. Government bonds gained alongside broad equity breadth rather than through a uniform retreat from risk assets.

The closing rate structure was equally selective. Five-year yields fell 1.08 basis points to 4.9291%, but two-year yields rose 0.42 basis point to 4.7761%. The 2s10s spread narrowed 3.54 basis points to 33.24, and 2s30s contracted 5.17 basis points to 64.37. The larger response in long maturities left short rates constrained by the continuing prospect of policy increases.

Over the week, 10-year yields were down 9.99 basis points and 30-year yields 13.71 basis points, compared with a decline of only 1.29 basis points at two years. The longer comparison still showed expensive financing: the 10-year yield was 11.15 basis points higher over the month and the 30-year 9.28 basis points higher. Tuesday's recovery reduced that burden but did not erase it.

At 10 years, the real yield fell 3.27 basis points to 2.7503%, while breakeven inflation rose 0.15 basis point to 2.3582%. The same division held over the week, with real yields down 11.12 basis points and breakevens up 1.13 basis points. Falling oil was an intraday catalyst, but the daily nominal rally came through lower real yields rather than a marked reduction in longer-run inflation compensation. That helps explain why the two-year maturity did not participate in the advance.

Bloomberg's Tuesday rates account said traders continued to fully price another Fed increase by year-end and a total of three by the end of next year, even after trimming expectations during the oil decline. The market was reassessing the amount and timing of restraint against weaker activity, while still allowing for additional tightening in response to inflation.

Housing supplied the clearest new evidence of that restraint. September starts fell 5.2% to an annualized 1.221 million, below the 1.30 million consensus and down from a revised 1.288 million in August. The previous monthly decline was revised to 5.9%. Construction therefore contracted again when economists had expected an increase in the level of starts.

Preliminary building permits were less weak. They declined 0.2% to 1.4 million from 1.403 million, but remained above the 1.39 million consensus. August permits had fallen 2.1%. The difference between a sharp reduction in groundbreakings and a much smaller decline in authorizations left the immediate deterioration concentrated in projects actually getting started, rather than in an equally abrupt collapse in the permit pipeline.

Transactions showed greater weakness. The National Association of Realtors' pending-home-sales index fell 7.3% to 66, its lowest since the series began in 2001. Economists had expected a 0.5% monthly decline after a 0.3% increase. The result was below every estimate in Bloomberg's survey. Contract signings fell across all regions, led by a 9.2% drop in the West and an 8.2% decline in the South, the largest home-selling region.

The calendar's year-on-year pending-sales measure declined 11.3%, following a 4.7% drop. NAR's separate unadjusted comparison put contract signings nearly 13% below a year earlier. Lawrence Yun, the association's chief economist, attributed September's deterioration to rapidly rising mortgage rates, with buyers and sellers holding back. Because contracts typically precede completed sales by a month or two, the decline also weakens the near-term outlook for closings.

The other U.S. releases pointed to moderation without establishing a broad contraction. Weekly ADP employment change slowed to 18,500 from 24,750. Redbook retail-sales growth eased to 9% year on year for the week ended October 17 from 10.4%. The Atlanta Fed's GDPNow estimate for Q3 edged down to 3.5% from 3.6%; that remained a model estimate of growth. Housing's particularly severe weakness sat beside continued growth in these broader indicators.

ING's Padhraic Garvey described the newly released U.S. data as broadly supportive of bonds. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent separately said he expected mortgage rates to decline once the energy shock passed. He also placed the administration's intended exit from conservatorship for Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac in next year or the following year. Neither prospect provided immediate relief to September's borrowers, whose financing costs had already curtailed construction and home purchases.

## AI Borrowing Pressure Reaches the Largest Issuers

Technology credit weakened even as long Treasury yields fell. Oracle default swaps traded as high as a record 343 basis points Tuesday, according to ICE Data Services cited by Bloomberg. Meta's credit-risk gauge rose as much as 6.3 basis points to a record 114.8 basis points ahead of Wednesday's earnings. Five-year protection on SpaceX reached an intraday record of 242 basis points early Tuesday, compared with around 111 basis points when its swaps began actively trading in June.

The common concern was the scale of the next financing round. Pimco strategist Lotfi Karoui said investors had yet to settle on how much debt markets would have to absorb for the AI buildout. Bloomberg's tally put worldwide borrowing to finance AI above $450 billion this year. With companies preparing to leave earnings blackout periods, existing bondholders were making room for prospective offerings rather than simply responding to an immediate deterioration in reported revenue.

Bank of America analysts estimated dealers bought a net $451 million of hyperscaler bonds Monday, their largest such accumulation since mid-September. They interpreted the inventory increase as likely reflecting investors reducing exposure because of supply concerns. Meta was expected by investors to sell bonds in the coming days, potentially ending a gap of more than two months in large technology companies' U.S. dollar issuance. SpaceX was discussing $40 billion of financing with banks and investors to purchase Nvidia chips, after raising $25 billion in its debut high-grade bond sale in June.

The expected Meta transaction remained an investor assessment. Its October 21 earnings date, earlier in the month than its customary last-Wednesday timing since 2022, had encouraged speculation that it was preserving a financing window before the November midterms. CreditSights analyst Jordan Chalfin had identified the possibility of a large post-earnings sale. The company had not responded to a request for comment.

Hedging activity showed how widely the exposure had spread. Barclays strategist Jigar Patel's analysis of trade-repository data put CDS trading tied to the ten largest hyperscalers and chipmakers at a record $140 billion through September, up 691% from about $17.7 billion in the same period of 2025. Some contracts had only recently begun trading. T. Rowe Price portfolio manager Steven Kohlenstein said growing financing requirements were making investors more conscious of correlated exposures across companies previously treated as separate credits.

The day's fresh equity setback came from Elice, whose shares fell 32% in their Seoul debut. The Korean computing supplier had government contracts, operating data centers and profitable operations, but was caught in the reassessment of neocloud financing. Its decline extended the pressure beyond companies still trying to bring their first projects into service. CoreWeave shares recovered Tuesday, while concern over its debt and the cost of financing expansion continued to frame the sector's reception.

There were also new signs that funding calendars were slipping. Blackstone-backed AirTrunk pushed planned investor discussions for a $1.5 billion Singapore real-estate investment trust into next year after September's U.S. rate increase. The proposed vehicle had been expected to offer a yield of roughly 6%. SB Energy's IPO talks had slowed substantially, with regulatory approvals taking longer than anticipated. Australia's market watchdog was gathering information about Firmus Grid's abandoned IPO, though it had not opened a formal investigation.

Those developments accompanied a widening divide between strong current semiconductor earnings and depressed valuations. Tuesday's Korean market account put the Kospi almost 40% below its June record, with Samsung and SK Hynix down 40% and 56%, respectively, from that peak. The companies together represented almost half the index's value. Samsung had earned a record $80 billion in the latest quarter, yet traded below five times estimated annual earnings; SK Hynix traded below four times. Both multiples were about half their decade averages. Investors were questioning how long customer spending could sustain those earnings, rather than disputing the current demand for memory.

After the U.S. equity close, SpaceX reported quarterly net income of $4.4 billion, above the $1.88 billion average analyst projection, with growth in its AI and satellite-internet businesses. Later coverage also said SpaceX and Tesla had formed special committees to explore a potential merger. Those earnings supplied an operating counterpoint to the day's record protection costs, while the committees opened a separate preliminary corporate process.

In a later update published at 5:35 p.m. New York time, Bloomberg relayed a Wall Street Journal account that Anthropic could spend $750 billion on additional computing power in coming years. The Journal, citing a draft IPO prospectus, also reported an $80.7 billion net loss in the first half of 2026. That prospective expenditure and historical loss added to the financing debate after the bond close, ahead of the company's planned public offering.

## France Pays More While Japanese Demand Revives

French government debt again moved against the broader recovery in core duration. The 10-year premium over Germany rose through 150 basis points and reached 154 during Tuesday trading, while the French yield moved back toward 5%. The spread remained below the month's 159-basis-point peak, but its renewed widening showed that quieter streets had not removed the fiscal pressure on the sovereign.

The protests had largely subsided after curfews and stronger security measures, yet resistance to spending restraint remained central to the government's financing problem. Morningstar DBRS insurance head Marcos Alvarez estimated the cost of the riots would, for now, remain below EUR1.2 billion. That damage estimate added a fresh measure of the weekend's disruption as France sought to contain its deficit and respond to living-cost demands.

ECB Governing Council member Olli Rehn attributed the spread widening to both international and country-specific pressures. Private-sector capital requirements, including AI investment, and larger public deficits were raising the cost of capital, he told Finnish lawmakers Tuesday. He said every euro-area country, including France and Finland, needed to control deficits to ensure debt sustainability. The intervention emphasized fiscal adjustment rather than promising support for French bonds.

BlackRock Investment Institute's Wei Li and colleagues likewise described the French selloff as evidence of intensifying competition for capital. Their comparison put more than 80% of global bonds above a 4% yield, against only 6.3% five years earlier. Borrowers faced a much larger set of competing investments. The institute also stressed that the euro area had stronger banks and more powerful ECB instruments than during the earlier sovereign crisis, while warning that intervention was not guaranteed. France's debt was nearly 120% of GDP, against around 89% for the euro area as a whole.

Bessent said Tuesday that he did not anticipate French turmoil spilling over into Treasuries and reported seeing a flight toward U.S. government debt from more concerning markets. That was his assessment of the current flows and risk. German and British debt also gained during the U.S. trading day: Bloomberg's later market account put their 10-year yields down 6 basis points to 3.40% and 2 basis points to 5.41%, respectively. France's widening premium occurred within a recovery elsewhere, sharpening its country-specific component.

Britain's new dealer survey quantified an approaching supply decision. The median of 11 forecasts put gilt issuance for the year through March at GBP249.2 billion, GBP3 billion above the GBP246.2 billion announced in April. Estimates ranged from GBP243 billion to GBP256.2 billion. Dealers expected fiscal headroom to fall by roughly a third to GBP15.2 billion, after partial offsets including higher bank levies, as increased debt costs and spending requirements narrowed the government's room for maneuver.

The expected change in composition was more pronounced than the increase in total gilts. Dealers projected GBP11.1 billion of Treasury bills, against GBP5 billion in April's plan. Short maturities were expected to account for 42.7% of gilt issuance and medium maturities 35.3%, up from 39% and 31%. Long-dated supply was expected at 6.5%, below the original 9%. Bank of America strategists Agne Stengeryte and Mark Capleton said a more substantial adjustment in maturity mix would better align supply with demand. These were forecasts for the October 28 budget and financing remit under Prime Minister Andy Burnham and Chancellor John Healey.

Japan supplied a realized demand result rather than a prospective supply revision. Tuesday's 20-year JGB auction drew a record bid-to-cover ratio of 5.84, up from 4.01 at the previous sale and a 12-month average of 3.73. The 20-year yield subsequently fell as much as 6 basis points to 3.710%, and the 30-year declined as much as 5 basis points. Elevated yields were attracting buyers in a segment that had recently suffered particularly sharp pressure.

The identity of those buyers remained debated. More than 83% of bids were attributed to unidentified investors. BNP Paribas Asset Management's Ryutaro Kimura saw that as suggesting large institutions, potentially including megabanks and the Government Pension Investment Fund. Deutsche Securities' Shoki Omori pointed to life insurers and pensions buying through trust banks, regional banks attracted by coupons, and dealer short covering. Bloomberg strategist Mark Cranfield suggested foreign participation. GPIF declined to discuss individual investment activity. Kimura also warned that banks could sell into falling yields and that recent equity declines could limit additional pension rebalancing demand.

Separately released figures established the scale of earlier domestic purchases. Japanese investors bought a net JPY18.8 trillion of government bonds in the six months ended September 30, the largest fiscal-first-half total in 17 years. Trust banks accounted for almost half and banks about a third. Mitsubishi UFJ Morgan Stanley Securities strategist Keisuke Tsuruta attributed much of the trust-bank buying to public-pension rebalancing after stronger equities and a weaker yen changed portfolio weights.

The foreign-bond figures showed why that domestic demand should not be read as a uniform withdrawal from overseas assets. Trust accounts bought JPY10.1 trillion of foreign bonds in the same half-year, while banks sold JPY7.4 trillion, their largest reduction since at least 2014. Tsuruta linked bank selling to expectations that expensive oil would push Treasury and European yields higher. Tuesday's release distinguished the behavior of banks from pension-related investors even as both contributed to demand for JGBs.

## Policy and Sovereign Funding Take Separate Paths

China moved from discussing an overnight policy benchmark to announcing a concrete period of operations. The PBOC said it would conduct overnight reverse repos from October 21 through November 2, extending beyond its previous concentration on month-end and tax-payment periods. The announcement supplied a practical next step in the proposed transition away from the seven-day benchmark.

Société Générale economist Michelle Lam said more frequent one-day operations would allow the central bank to test transmission and reduce short-rate volatility. Tianfeng Securities analysts led by Liu Jie expected the overnight rate to become the formal benchmark in the first half of 2027. Nanhua Futures researcher Gao Xiang said increased frequency and more transparent pricing were still needed before the transition could be completed.

The easing interpretation remained contested. Analysts saw a lower funding anchor as potentially supporting bond carry and encouraging purchases further along the curve, while more reliable overnight refinancing could also increase leverage and maturity mismatches. China's one-year interest-rate swap fell to its lowest since 2009. But a Tuesday Financial News article, published by a PBOC-affiliated newspaper, cited GF Securities economist Guo Lei arguing that reform of the operating framework should not be equated with a rate cut. The announced operations and the expected formal timetable were firmer developments than any conclusion about the eventual policy stance.

Hungary delivered an actual hold, keeping its benchmark at 5.5% for a second month, as all 22 economists surveyed by Bloomberg expected. Governor Mihaly Varga described the government's fiscal path as consistent with eventual euro entry, while reiterating a cautious, data-dependent policy approach. The plan targets a deficit of 4.9% of GDP next year and 2.8% in 2030. Prime Minister Peter Magyar said euro adoption should come as soon as possible but set no date.

The budget received a muted market response after investors had already priced substantial consolidation and progress toward the single currency. With September inflation at 1.6%, below the central bank's 2%-4% tolerance band, fiscal credibility and the forint's response were important to the scope for renewed easing. Varga said the government would have to decide subsequent steps, including entry into the ERM-2 exchange-rate mechanism.

Polish Monetary Policy Council member Marcin Zarzecki supplied unusually specific tightening conditions. He said he did not expect a November increase but would not exclude one. Two developments among persistent core inflation above 3.5% for two months, wage growth above 7%, and a zloty exchange rate weaker than 4.5 per euro would warrant serious consideration of a 25-basis-point rise. Three conditions could support a series of increases or a larger single move. Removal of fuel-price caps or higher household energy tariffs for 2027 were additional political risks he identified.

The latest readings remained below those thresholds: core inflation was 3.1%, August wage growth 5.6%, and the currency had traded at 4.37 per euro Monday. Zarzecki said his views matched Governor Adam Glapinski's, contrasting with fellow policymaker Przemyslaw Litwiniuk's assessment last week that the zloty remained strong. Zarzecki also warned that proceedings against Glapinski could expose policy decisions to legal challenges; the governor rejected the allegations of political interference as baseless.

Indonesia's immediate policy pressure was different. By late Tuesday, 19 of 38 economists expected Wednesday's decision to raise the 5.75% benchmark: 17 anticipated 25 basis points and two expected 50. The change in forecasts followed currency and bond pressure after MSCI's reclassification warning. Indonesian stocks rebounded Tuesday, with the Jakarta benchmark gaining as much as 4.3% after authorities promised changes. The exchange said highly concentrated companies would be excluded from the benchmark calculation following discussions with MSCI, while concerns about ownership transparency and coordinated trading persisted.

Senegal's dollar bonds instead responded to a fresh obstacle to an agreed financing path. The 2031 notes fell 2.10 cents to 49.99 cents by 2:45 p.m. in London Tuesday; the 2033 and 2048 securities dropped as much as 2 cents. Parliamentary speaker and opposition leader Ousmane Sonko threatened to withhold approval of the revised 2026 budget and next year's spending plan, objecting to subsidy reductions designed to cap fuel support at 1% of GDP by 2028.

Sonko's Pastef party holds a parliamentary majority, giving the dispute direct consequences for passage. Senegal is seeking board approval for a $2.2 billion IMF facility agreed in principle last month while restructuring external obligations under the G20 Common Framework. Standard Chartered's Samir Gadio attributed its underperformance to uncertainty over the budget. Budget Minister Bassirou Sarr defended the plan by citing higher energy costs and the need to protect salaries and existing social commitments. The financing timetable now faced a political obstacle to delivering the adjustment, not simply a disagreement over its numerical ambition.

Brazil was preparing an additional funding channel. Officials were in China working on a debut panda-bond sale that could begin as early as next week, according to a person familiar with the plans. The target was around CNY10 billion, starting with CNY5 billion, which would make Brazil the first Latin American sovereign to issue in that market. Treasury said there was no fixed date and execution would depend on conditions and demand.

The possible launch follows the October 25 presidential runoff. The person familiar with preparations expected the initial transaction to proceed even if Flavio Bolsonaro won, although the longer-term strategy of expanding Chinese issuance could differ under him and President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva. Vale was also considering yuan debt and intended to continue regardless of the result, according to a person familiar with its plans. The sovereign has raised about $10 billion internationally this year and is seeking authorization for up to $35 billion annually, making the Chinese preparation part of a broader diversification of external borrowing.

Romania separately ended months of political impasse when Luca Niculescu won parliamentary approval for a new cabinet Tuesday. The fourth premier nominated since May now faces the task of maintaining fiscal discipline, convincing rating agencies and reviving growth after the deadlock weighed on the currency. The confidence vote resolved the government-formation problem while leaving the fiscal program to be delivered.

## Refinancing Terms Expose Credit Dispersion

Radiology Partners withdrew a proposed $485 million add-on to its 2032 loan and switched to marketing junk bonds, according to a person familiar with the financing. The bonds were being discussed at a yield as high as 10.25%, against an 8.38% average for similarly rated securities tracked by Bloomberg. The abandoned loan had offered a margin of as much as 475 basis points above the benchmark and a price as low as 98 cents. That floating-rate margin and discounted issue price were different components from the all-in yield on the replacement bond.

The acquisition financing added to signs of difficulty in loan syndication. Grant Thornton Advisors had replaced a $500 million-equivalent euro loan with bonds Monday, while AVI-SPL withdrew a $690 million refinancing. Envestnet had to improve terms Tuesday on a $625 million loan for its Vestmark acquisition. Borrowers had valued loans' ability to be refinanced without bond-style early-redemption penalties, but weaker demand and floating-rate debt service were complicating execution.

Some investors were responding by examining the highest-rated part of high yield rather than abandoning corporate risk altogether. T. Rowe Price and Invesco were considering BB debt after the recent selloff, with managers emphasizing cash generation, margins and lower leverage. S&P data cited in the reporting put three-year cumulative defaults at 4.17% for BB borrowers, compared with 0.91% for BBB, 12.41% for B and 45.67% for CCC. Moody's research found distressed borrowers accounted for about a third of high-yield maturities over the next two years. Those comparisons explain the quality distinction behind the interest in BB securities, while broad U.S. high-yield spreads were little changed on the day.

PLS demonstrated that issuance remained possible. The Australian lithium producer raised $700 million of 2032 notes at par to yield 8%. Proceeds are for general corporate purposes, including investment and growth, after approval earlier this month of an A$1.9 billion expansion intended almost to double capacity at Pilgangoora. Moody's assigned Ba3 Tuesday, citing negative cash flow and increased debt during construction, as well as greater exposure to weak lithium prices. The company had paid 6.875% on its first dollar bond sale in April, a separate transaction in a different financing environment.

CIBC also converted a previously marketed offering into completed terms. It sold C$1 billion of additional-tier-one limited recourse capital notes Monday at 297 basis points over government debt, with a 6.631% coupon and 43 buyers, according to people familiar with the deal. The 60-year instruments are first callable after about five years, with subsequent five-year redemption opportunities. Early repayment requires regulatory approval. Bloomberg Intelligence's Himanshu Bakshi warned that extension risk was rising as banks weighed replacement costs, capital needs and reset spreads.

Pernod Ricard sought a different form of balance-sheet support, beginning investor calls for its first hybrid issue alongside a capped tender across seven senior euro bonds totaling EUR4.7 billion. The proposed perpetual tranches would be first callable after 5.25 and eight years. Its net-debt-to-EBITDA ratio stood at 3.7 times, against a target below three by fiscal 2029, and both Moody's Baa1 and S&P's BBB+ senior ratings carried negative outlooks. Expected hybrid ratings were Baa3 and BBB-. Partial equity credit from rating agencies was important to the proposal, with the market's hybrid-over-senior spread at 61 basis points, near record lows and below a long-run average above 120.

Thames Water and supporting creditors offered Pimco a revised allocation of GBP2.4 billion of additional rescue debt. The proposal would distribute the first GBP600 million proportionately among super-senior, Class A and Class B creditors, then allocate the remaining GBP1.8 billion across the expanded super-senior group. That would give Pimco and other existing top-ranking lenders a larger share than the original allocation, addressing concern about dilution as the facility increased to GBP5.4 billion.

The facility carries a 9.75% coupon plus fees and trades above face value. Thames says the additional funding would sustain operations through autumn 2027. The allocation compromise seeks creditor support ahead of an October 29 vote, which could finish sooner if the required majority approves. The Class A group's separate recapitalization and takeover plan still requires the regulator and government to be persuaded, while the government has considered special administration. The new offer concerned access to rescue funding and the distribution of its senior claims.

Vestel launched a restructuring proposal with a direct choice over principal and maturity. Holders could exchange up to $250 million of its $500 million 2029 issue for 2032 notes worth 55 cents per dollar and carrying a 6% coupon, accepting a 45% haircut. Alternatively, they could preserve principal with maturity extended to 2035 and interest reduced to 4%. A November 11 meeting requires support from at least 75% of represented bonds. The Turkish appliance producer is separately negotiating domestic bank debt amid weaker earnings and liquidity pressure.

Huachen Energy disclosed repayment difficulties on $956 million due in December, attributing them on a Friday creditor call to disappointing earnings, asset-sale problems and limited assistance from parent Wintime Energy. The Chinese power producer was seeking another six-year extension after its earlier restructuring and planned individual creditor discussions this week. The obligations include roughly $627 million of dollar notes and CNY2.2 billion of yuan bonds. The latest proposal would defer a payment deadline already extended after its 2021 default.

WestJet's 8% 2031 bonds traded near 85 cents Tuesday morning, down around 3% from Monday and at their lowest since issuance in June. Expensive fuel, U.S.-Canada trade uncertainty and disruption from August's flight-attendant strike weighed on the outlook after S&P's September downgrade to B-. The price was around 95 cents in early October. In Australia, Ares executive Peter Graf separately warned that floating-rate property lending faced increasing stress, with senior real-estate loans now potentially costing 11%-12%, against 8%-9% six months earlier. He and Blackstone's Mark Glengarry did not expect a systemic credit squeeze, distinguishing pressure in individual property exposures from the broader regional credit outlook.

Municipal transactions showed stronger access for some smaller borrowers. Chapin School priced a $25 million refinancing at 47 basis points over its benchmark, with demand five times the initial offer, according to its spokesperson. It will use its own funds to repay the other half of $50 million coming due, reducing outstanding debt by a third. Its A+ rating, $128 million investment portfolio and strong admissions demand accompanied operating deficits the school attributed primarily to $13 million of noncash depreciation. Ontario International Airport planned roughly $174 million of bonds for terminal and runway work after Fitch upgraded its debt two notches to A+; around $124 million would be subject to the alternative minimum tax.

## Forward Market Significance

Wednesday's mortgage applications will put a more recent financing-demand observation beside September's housing contraction. The preceding MBA survey showed a 7.5% 30-year mortgage rate and applications down 2.7%. Thursday's initial jobless claims, expected at 200,000, and continuing claims, expected at 1.720 million, will extend the labor comparison after slower weekly ADP hiring. The question is whether housing's sharp deterioration remains concentrated in the most rate-sensitive activity or accompanies a wider loss of momentum.

The October 21 20-year Treasury auction and October 22 five-year TIPS sale will test demand after the long-end rally and the decline in real yields. Nominal and inflation-linked buyers face different exposures: Tuesday's 10-year breakeven barely moved even as real yields fell. At the same time, prospective technology issuance will compete for capital, with Meta's Wednesday earnings providing the next current update on spending and a possible opening for new borrowing.

Friday's October flash S&P Global PMIs will broaden the activity assessment. Manufacturing consensus is 55.5 after 55.9, and services 58 after 58.8. Final Michigan figures carry expected inflation readings of 4.7% over one year and 3.5% over five years. Continued activity growth alongside elevated expectations would leave a different Fed tradeoff from a broad slowdown with easing price expectations, particularly after the front end resisted Tuesday's duration rally.

Energy retains an independent capacity to change that assessment. API reported a 4.93 million-barrel crude-stock draw Tuesday afternoon, larger than the 1.3 million decline expected, following a revised 11.12 million draw. Wednesday's EIA crude figure is expected to show a 0.3 million-barrel decline. Diplomatic talks remain active, while European gas supplied a separate warning Tuesday: benchmark Dutch futures rose as much as 2.4% to EUR90.16 per megawatt-hour, their highest since December 2022. Ryanair chief Michael O'Leary forecast fares could rise as much as 20% next year as fuel costs pass through, with most European airlines lacking substantial hedges for that period.

Bank Indonesia's decision is due Wednesday at 2 p.m. Jakarta time, with economists evenly divided on whether the benchmark rises. The response of the rupiah and government debt will matter alongside the rate decision as authorities address the underlying equity-market governance concerns. Korea's Thursday decision offers a different test: all 24 surveyed economists expect a hold at 3%, but Citi and Nomura see further increases toward 3.5%. September headline and core inflation were 2.9% and 2.8%, still above the 2% target. Governor Shin Hyun Song's assessment of the equity rout against strong semiconductor exports, and any dissent for an immediate increase, will shape expectations for November.

Britain's October 28 budget will turn the new dealer forecasts into an actual borrowing remit and maturity mix. In France, renewed spread widening leaves fiscal agreement and the political response to living-cost pressure unresolved despite quieter protests. Japan's auction has demonstrated demand at elevated yields, but the competing explanations for the buying leave its persistence dependent on how domestic institutions respond to subsequent market moves. Across these markets, the next change in financing conditions will come from concrete supply decisions, policy choices and creditor agreements rather than the direction of Treasury yields alone.

overall_summary.headline: Long Treasuries rally on weaker housing and falling oil, while corporate financing strains persist
overall_summary.session_narrative:
Longer-dated Treasuries recovered part of Monday's selloff as oil retreated and September housing data showed high borrowing costs curtailing construction and transactions. The 10-year yield fell 3.12 basis points to 5.1085% and the 30-year declined 4.75 basis points to 5.4198%, while the 2-year rose 0.42 basis point to 4.7761%. The 2s10s curve narrowed 3.54 basis points to 33.24 basis points. The rally came through real yields: the 10-year real yield fell 3.27 basis points to 2.7503%, while breakeven inflation rose 0.15 basis point to 2.3582%.

Housing starts dropped 5.2% to an annualized 1.221 million, and pending home sales fell 7.3% to a record-low index reading of 66. Oil's reversal accelerated the bond recovery, but negotiations over the Iran war had produced no agreement and energy remained expensive. Traders continued to fully price another Fed increase by year-end.

The improvement in government borrowing costs did not resolve corporate financing pressure. Oracle, Meta and SpaceX protection costs reached records as investors anticipated more AI borrowing. Radiology Partners abandoned a loan add-on for bonds discussed at yields as high as 10.25%, while Thames Water revised creditors' allocation of rescue debt. Broad U.S. high-yield spreads were little changed. France's premium over Germany widened even as other core government bonds gained, underscoring the distinction between demand for duration and confidence in individual borrowers.
